previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic pancreatitis, and asthma was readmitted for worsening epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting after a recent relapse in alcohol use. He presented unable to tolerate oral intake, with elevated liver enzymes and an anion gap metabolic acidosis that improved with IV fluids. Imaging confirmed fatty liver, splenomegaly, and portal flow reversal consistent with cirrhosis and portal hypertension, but no acute cholecystitis. His pain was managed with IV then oral hydromorphone, and his diet was advanced as symptoms improved. Liver function tests trended toward improvement by discharge, and he remained asymptomatic for alcohol withdrawal. He was discharged home on his baseline medications, including nadolol, spironolactone, lactulose, and omeprazole, with 30 tablets of oral hydromorphone for short-term pain control, and follow-up arranged with primary care and liver clinic. Social work assisted with addiction support planning.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with ___ asthma, alcoholic cirrhosis presented initially

# hypercarbic resp failure: h/o asthma and supposedly presented 
to PCP with wheezing, cough, SOB, chest tightness. did not 
respond to po prednisone given by PCP. on ___ presented to OSH 
with sats 94% RA, RR 22, wheezing. continued to worsen with

- no obvious PNA. Required paralysis to ventilate at OSH and 
upon transfer to BI as well (used rocuronium at ___. Treated

montelukast, and loratadine. Noted to have elevated IgE at OSH 
which supported asthma diagnosis. Obtained CT chest here which 
was not suggestive of ABPA or COPD. Had fevers so despite neg 
CXR started pt on levofloxacin for presumed atypical PNA or CAP. 
Also did a bronch and BAL. BAL was positive for influenza B, 
MSSA and serratia. Pt was out of window for treatment with 
tamiflu. He improved on levofloxacin and defervesced and was 
extubated on ___. Transferred to the floor on ___.  He 
completed his course of oral steroids and levofloxacin prior to 
discharge.  He was quickly weaned to room air.  He will 
follow-up with a new outpatient pulmonologist.

# EtOH cirrhosis: possible liver mass seen on prior u/s. AFP has

febrile) and spirono (for hyperkalemia). Restarted when

hepatologist for repeat imaging and management of his alcoholic

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History of asthma exacerbation.  Please evaluate.

COMPARISONS:  None.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal AP radiograph of the chest x-ray.

FINDINGS:  The ET tube terminates approximately 3.2 cm above the carina. 
There is an enteric tube which extends below the diaphragm with the tip in the
body of the stomach.  The lungs are clear without evidence of focal
consolidations concerning for pneumonia.  There is mild bibasilar atelectasis.
There is no large pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  The visualized osseous
structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intrathoracic abnormalities identified.  ET tube
terminates approximately 3.2 cm above the carina.

HISTORY:  History of cirrhosis and possible hepatic mass with recent weight
gain concerning for ascites.  Evaluate for hepatic mass and/or ascites.  

COMPARISON:  None at this institution. 

FINDINGS:

The liver is slightly nodular echotexture, in keeping with known cirrhosis. 
Adjacent to the gallbladder fossa within the right hepatic lobe, there is a
geographic area of relatively hypoechoic hepatic parenchyma, possibly an area
of focal fatty sparing, although an infiltrative mass cannot be excluded.  No
additional focal hepatic lesions are identified.  There is no intra or
extrahepatic biliary duct dilatation, with common duct measuring 5 mm.  The
portal vein is patent, with normal hepatopetal flow.  The gallbladder is
unremarkable.  The visualized portion of the pancreas is unremarkable.  The
left-most portion of the pancreatic tail was not well assessed due to
overlying bowel gas.  The spleen is enlarged, measuring 16.9 cm.  There is no
free fluid in the abdomen.  

IMPRESSION:

1. Findings compatible with cirrhosis and portal hypertension, including
moderate splenomegaly. 

2. Geographic area of hypoechoic hepatic parenchyma in the right hepatic lobe,
adjacent to the gallbladder fossa.  While this could represent an area of
focal fatty sparing, given the patient's history of cirrhosis, an infiltrative
hepatic mass such as hepatocellular carcinoma cannot be excluded.  Further
evaluation with MRI is recommended. 

3. No ascites.

PORTABLE CHEST FILM ___ AT 4:30 A.M. 

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ with asthma, intubated, assess for interval
change.

Comparison to ___ at 1408

A portable AP upright chest film ___ at 4:30 a.m. is submitted.

IMPRESSION:

1.  A right subclavian PICC line now has its tip in the mid SVC.  An
endotracheal tube has its tip approximately 4 cm above the carina.  A
nasogastric tube is seen coursing below the diaphragm with the tip projecting
over the stomach.  Lungs remain somewhat diminished but are without evidence
of focal airspace consolidation, pleural effusions, pneumothorax or pulmonary
edema.  Overall cardiac and mediastinal contours are within normal limits.

INDICATION:  Cirrhosis and obstructive hypercarbic respiratory failure. 
Assess for airway disease.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous helical MDCT images were obtained through the chest
without IV contrast.  Multiplanar axial, coronal, sagittal and maximum
intensity projection axial images were generated.

TOTAL BODY DLP:  616 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:  Although this study is not designed for assessment of the
subdiaphragmatic structures, the visualized solid organs and stomach are
within normal limits, however, the spleen is enlarged up to 15 cm.  There are
perisplenic varices.  An enteric tube has its tip and side port in the
stomach.

CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST:  The partially visualized thyroid is unremarkable. 
There is no supraclavicular, axillary, hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. 
The patient is intubated.  The ET tube terminates 2.6 cm from the carina. 
Right PICC line terminates in the SVC.  Enteric tube courses through the
esophagus.

The central airways are patent.  There is mild bronchial wall thickening and
minimal mucus plugging, particularly at the lung bases which may reflect small
airways disease.  The heart is not enlarged. Trace pericardial fluid is likely
within normal limits, physiologic.  There is no pneumothorax or pleural
effusion.  There is mild atelectasis at the left base.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Mild bronchial wall thickening and mucus plugging at the lung bases may
reflect small airway disease.
2.  Minimal left lower lobe atelectasis.
3.  Nodular liver compatible with history of cirrhosis with perisplenic
varices and splenomegaly.
